text:
morgan: heads-up — Q3 demand model just landed. marketing conflates two campaigns, looks like a 22–35% uplift in peak gpu-hours for ~6 weeks starting mid-july. we need to talk packing and fairness before the surge.

alex: ouch. do we have region breakdown? APAC vs NA?

morgan: APAC heavy (campaign localized), but NA still sees background growth from search embeddings. APAC peak windows cluster 02:00–07:00 UTC which aligns with our US evening.

rachel: can you paste the forecast numbers?

morgan: summary from the model:
- baseline steady-state 1.0x
- median peak uplift 1.28x
- 95th percentile peak ~1.35x
- expected concurrent tenants above 90% capacity for ~10 rolling days in worst week
- likely heavier fragmentation on pools with mixed A100/H100 nodes

morgan: link to raw CSV: S3://redwood-ops/forecasts/q3_campaign_v2.csv (internal)

jia: immediate asks: 1) do we need short-term reserve or cross-region bursting? 2) can we reduce fragmentation via defrag compaction? 3) fairshare weight tweaks?

sam: for (1) cross-region bursting is viable but networking egress + latency for embeddings matters. we should only burst non-latency-sensitive routes.

vikram: defrag compaction helps but it's disruptive if we drain running slots. propose a canary: pick one medium pool, run compaction with preemption budget 10% and monitor evictions.

alex: what about slot-slicing — give more tenants 1/2-slices instead of 1-slot allocations for small requests? reduces internal fragmentation at the cost of throughput.

rachel: we have a slice prototype from last quarter. metrics showed 15% better slot utilization for small workloads but increased scheduling overhead in the runtime. we can try it on bursty APAC pools.

morgan: propose short plan:
- schedule compaction canary next Tue on pool-apac-medium (preempt-budget=10%)
- enable slice scheduling for small-requests feature flag on same pool
- keep a 5% reserve of H100 capacity in NA for latency-critical fallbacks
- allow cross-region burst for batch embedding jobs only (route-level policy)

jia: +1. need telemetry added: per-tenant fragmentation metric, preemptions, tail-latency, slot-utilization, and eviction-count. add an alert if fragmentation delta > 8% over baseline.

devops-bot: Reminder: scheduled job created — compaction-canary pool-apac-medium starts 2024-07-02T09:00:00Z. Runbook link: https://confluence/internal/compaction-canary

sam: cost callout — cross-region egress could add ~$20k/week at projected burst rates, but prevents 50% of user-facing timeouts for embeddings. tradeoff: cash vs SLA.

vikram: also consider affinity packing: prefer colocation of tenants with similar model sizes to reduce leftover fragments. heuristic: sort by requested vram desc and best-fit decreasing. low-risk to enable as scheduling policy toggle.

alex: can we run a simulation on historical traces with the campaign spike injected? want numbers before flipping policies.

morgan: yes — i'll queue a sim job. target: run overnight, share results tomorrow.

rachel: if sim shows >12% reclaimable via compaction+slice, we flip canary->wide in 48 hours. else, hold and provision short-term reserved nodes.

morgan: thanks all. action items:
- alex: run sim on traces (due 24h)
- vikram: implement affinity toggle + compile opt plan (48h)
- sam: estimate cross-region egress cost more precisely and list candidate routes (24h)
- jia: add telemetry probes and fragmentation alert (24h)
- rachel: monitor canary once started and call rollback if eviction tail spikes > 2x baseline (on-call)

sam: noted. I'll also draft a condensed note for finance with cost vs SLA options.

morgan: will post simulation id here when available. :thumbsup:
